facts.big: I don’t feel well. · I have a…
facts.label: Dizer que está mal
facts.sub: Diga I don’t feel well. I have a sore throat. Descreva I have chills. Peça Can I have some tissues? Pergunte Are there any lozenges? e peça Can you call my boss?

facts.label: Época de resfriados
facts.sub: No inverno, muitos americanos pegam resfriado. Eles ficam em casa, bebem muito líquido e usam lenços. Se a febre não passa, ligam para o médico ou vão à clínica.

facts.label: Remédios caseiros
facts.sub: Chá com mel, sopa quente e repouso são comuns. O chá de gengibre e o limão também ajudam. Os americanos chamam isso de home remedies, remédios feitos em casa.

pages.title: A day in bed · 1/3
paragraphs: It is a gray Monday morning in Tampa. Ian wakes up in his bed with a heavy head. He sneezes two times and his eyes are red. His throat is sore, his voice is hoarse, and his nose is stuffy. He thinks it is the flu, and he walks slowly to the kitchen. His roommate Ruby is making toast and looks at him.
“You look pale. Are you okay?” says Ruby. “I don’t feel well. I have a sore throat and a stuffy nose.” says Ian. “Do you have a fever? Let me get the thermometer.” says Ruby.

pages.title: A day in bed · 3/3
paragraphs: “Can you call my boss? I can’t talk well.” says Ian. “Of course. Get some sleep and feel better soon!” says Ruby. Ruby brings a thermometer and a box of tissues. Ian has a small fever, so he goes back to bed, and Ruby turns on the humidifier. She makes a cup of hot ginger tea with honey, an old family remedy. She finds a few lozenges in a drawer. Then she calls his boss and explains everything. Ian drinks the tea, closes his eyes and sleeps.
